KEY MESSAGE 1...Another frosty morning expected today, 
especially inland but milder mornings are just around the 
corner. While probabilities are low, we will have to watch out 
for any freezing fog that may form tonight. Kept it out of the 
forecast for now, but observations will be closely monitored. 
Later today low- level thicknesses increasing supports steady 
warming, and even though high pressure will remain in place, 
temps will warm to above climo with 70s inland through FRI. For
the OBX, highs will be tempered by light northeast breezes off 
the cooler waters of the Labrador Current as water temps have 
cooled to the upper 50s. 

In addition to moderating temperatures, we will remain dry with
high pressure settling overhead by the end of the week, and off
the coast by Saturday. Fire weather concerns may grow with the 
curing vegetation combined with low RH values each afternoon. 
Luckily winds will not be an issue with a light gradient in 
place. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Confidence is high on a low developing off the
FL coast Fri/Sat and gaining strength in response to a 
shortwave digging across the Gulf above SFC coastal troughing 
ongoing along the FL leg of the Gulfstream. However, what 
happens once a pressure center presents itself remains fairly 
uncertain with the typical questions for a low that hasn't even
formed yet off the coast: where the system will track, how much
it deepens, how fast is it moving, etc... What 
structure/characteristics the low will have is also in question 
with NHC offering up 60% chance that this low could take on 
subtropical, and maybe even tropical characteristics. The key 
point here is: the impacts will not change based on what this 
low ends up being called. Initially a generally Nward motion is 
expected. Overnight model suites still show a wide swath of 
solutions, with some back and forth between possible solutions 
even within the same model. Wrn solutions continue shifting a
bit further east, with the vast majority of ensemble guidance
suggesting the center of the low moves through between the 
NC/VA border and ~40 miles offshore of Cape Hatteras. Details 
will become clearer over the next 24-36hrs as we get into the 
HiRes window, get more data on the upper level pattern 
progression, see how convection over the Gulf and Sern 
Gulfstream plays out, and get closer to actual cyclogenesis. 
Bottom line even though we are a day closer, nothing has been 
ironed out! 

KEY MESSAGE 3...King Tide Cycle starts second half of this 
weekend, peaking middle of next week. This higher than normal 
astronomical tide cycle is slightly stronger than the one that 
occurred the last week of OCT. Will have to see how the system 
in Key Message 2 and the potential wind increase in Key Message
4 play out before we can determine what sort of effect this 
King Tide cycle will have on our coast.

KEY MESSAGE 4...In the wake of this weekend's low, a high
briefly builds in early next week. Mid-week, models indicate a  
deepening trough moving through the Gulf states and progressing
offshore of the SE US. This shortwave may encounter a stationary
boundary offshore of SE US and the baroclinic zone along the
Gulf Stream and produce a sfc short wave or low. The pressure
gradient would tighten considerably in this scenario, with the
high sitting over the NE. Confidence is LOW at this point, but 
if materialized, a period of higher wind and seas is possible, 
coinciding with the peak of King Tides (See Key Message 3). We 
will have to see how this weekend's low plays out, until then
the confidence will remain low for the forecast mid next week.
